cases.statement: Three family members in one case report (PMID 32477554) carry the variant, all heterozygous: the 7-year-old proband and his 5-year-old brother (both with recurrent sterile arthritis) and their asymptomatic father. The 2021 review (PMID 34745107) lists the same case report's proband as one row in its treatment table with no further genotype detail. All three family members also carry two other PSTPIP1 intronic variants (c.36+68 G>A and c.137+47 G>C).

people.key_phenotypes: recurrent suppurative (culture-negative) knee arthritis; no pyoderma, acne, hidradenitis or fever; raised ESR and CRP; markedly raised IL-6 with normal IL-1beta; responded to tocilizumab

quotes.quote: A 7-year-old boy of Han ethnicity, weighing 23.5 kg, was admitted to hospital with recurrent episodes of joint swelling and severe pain for 1 year.
He had two surgeries in the prior year for suppurative knee arthritis.
There was no obvious trauma before the onset of each episode, and no pyoderma, acne, suppurative hidradenitis, systemic infection, or fever during the course of the disease.
No bacterial growth was observed in either culture of articular cavity effusion (microbiology cultures were saved for 28 days).
Interestingly, the patient displayed a markedly high level of IL-6, while his IL-1 and other cytokines were not elevated.

phenotype_specificity.statement: The proband and brother have recurrent sterile arthritis only, without the skin features of the classic triad; the authors call it an incomplete presentation. Autoimmune antibodies, RF and HLA-B27 were negative, joint cultures were sterile, and PAMI was considered unlikely on clinical grounds. No other genes were reported as tested and the genetic testing method (panel, exome or single gene) is not stated.

quotes.quote: Although this boy’s clinical presentation is incomplete, possibly due to young age of both brothers, we still tend to diagnose him as having an auto-inflammatory disease such as PAPA syndrome rather than juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) for several reasons.

(2) Autoimmune antibodies such as AKA, ANA, anti-dsDNA antibodies, anti-Smith antibodies, and ANCA were all negative, as were RF and HLA-B27, so other autoimmune rheumatic diseases, including JIA, were not supported.

PSTPIP1-associated myeloid-related proteinemia inflammatory syndrome (PAMI), another kind of auto-inflammatory disease, could also be eliminated because of the absence of neutropenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia, and liver or spleen enlargement.
Maybe we can call it incomplete PAPA syndrome with elevated IL-6.
The clinical features of PAPA syndrome include fever, acne, pyoderma gangrenosum, joint swelling, and pain.

segregation.statement: Two affected brothers carry the variant (1 affected relative of the proband). The father carries it and is unaffected. The grandfather, who had recurrent pyoderma, declined testing; the paper does not say whether he is the paternal or maternal grandfather. The mother is not mentioned. The two co-occurring intronic variants were found in the same three people.

quotes.quote: the patient, his brother, and his father were all heterozygous for the PSTPIP1 gene mutation, which was found in the exon region (c.36+68 G>A, c.137+47 G>C, and c.562+114C>G het)
Although the father was a carrier, he never showed signs of the syndrome.
The boy’s grandfather also had a history of recurrent pyoderma.
The grandfather declined genetic testing.

The two boys’ clinical manifestations were also different from those of their grandfather, who only had recurrent pyoderma, while their father, who also carried the gene mutation, exhibited no symptoms.

de_novo.statement: Not de novo in the proband or brother: the father carries the variant. The mother's testing is not reported.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Intronic substitution 114 nucleotides into the intron after coding position c.562 (deep intronic; predicted protein effect p.? per the batch HGVS). The case report nevertheless describes the variants as 'found in the exon region'. Disease mechanism as stated in the papers: PSTPIP1 mutations increase affinity for pyrin and drive inflammasome/IL-1 activation.

quotes.quote: This mutation leads to an increased affinity for pyrin, leading to up-regulation of caspase 1 and activation of interleukin-1 (IL-1), which produces a neutrophil-mediated response.

Mutations in the PSTPIP1 gene influence the ability of PSTPIP1 to phosphorylate proinflammatory pyrin domains, leading to the accumulation, activation, and reduced inhibition of the inflammasome, release of IL-1β and IL-18, activation of caspase 1, and dysregulated downstream TNF-α production in mononuclear cells (8).

population_data_in_papers.statement: The authors state the variant was not reported in the normal genome database (database not named), whereas the two co-occurring intronic variants were frequent in 1000 normal subjects.

quotes.quote: These three mutated sites have not been reported in the previous literature, among which the first and second mutated sites were highly expressed in the sequencing of 1000 normal subjects, while the third mutated site was not reported in the normal genome database, so it may be a possible deleterious mutated site.

authors_classification.statement: The authors call it novel and 'a possible deleterious mutated site'; no ACMG criteria are stated. The review (PMID 34745107) lists it without comment.

quotes.quote: These three mutated sites have not been reported in the previous literature, among which the first and second mutated sites were highly expressed in the sequencing of 1000 normal subjects, while the third mutated site was not reported in the normal genome database, so it may be a possible deleterious mutated site.
The mutation site of PSTPIP1 in this incomplete PAPA syndrome has not been reported before.

concerns: The variant is intronic (c.562+114), but the case report says the three variants were 'found in the exon region'; the paper contradicts its own HGVS.
No transcript is stated in either paper; the batch's NM_003978.5 is an assumption.
The 'het' after the three variants could apply to all three or only to c.562+114C>G; the sentence says the three people were 'all heterozygous for the PSTPIP1 gene mutation'.
The same people carry two other PSTPIP1 intronic variants (c.36+68 G>A, c.137+47 G>C), which the authors say were frequent in 1000 normal subjects.
The heterozygous father is unaffected (the authors invoke incomplete penetrance); the affected grandfather was not tested.
The genetic testing method and whether any other genes were examined are not stated.
Phenotype is incomplete for PAPA (arthritis only, no pyoderma gangrenosum or acne) and the IL-6-predominant profile differs from the IL-1-mediated mechanism the papers describe.

PAPA-ID0119 (review table row in PMID 34745107, 'Guo, Y. N. (2) | 1') is very likely the same person as PAPA-ID0044 (the proband of PMID 32477554): the review cites the Guo 2020 case report as its reference 2, and the row's variants and treatment (MTX, CS, tocilizumab) match. The pipeline did not merge them.
The review (PMID 34745107) only lists the variant in a treatment table with no case description.
The case report says PAPA syndrome was 'first reported in 2012', whereas the review says it was first described in 1997; a minor inaccuracy in the case report's background.
notes_for_panel: One family, one case report (PMID 32477554, read in full); the review (PMID 34745107) adds only a table row that repeats the same proband. No functional, splicing or in-silico evidence is reported for this deep intronic variant. Elevated IL-6 is a patient laboratory finding, not an assay of the variant.
